note: Acute coronary syndrome, unselected: the class relied on rat AV-shunt/FeCl3 and dog Folts thrombosis models with bleeding time plus ex vivo ADP aggregation; every ACS efficacy prediction held, and FDA read ticagrelor's dyspnoea as foreshadowed by rat safety pharmacology.
label: ACS (P2Y12)

engagement.model: Rat ex vivo ADP-induced platelet aggregation
engagement.note: Clopidogrel (PCR 4099) given orally abolished ADP-induced aggregation in washed rat platelets; no patient comparison yet.
engagement.short: Clopidogrel abolishes ADP aggregation in rats
engagement.quote: Besides a complete suppression of the ADP-induced aggregation, the two drugs significantly inhibited aggregation and secretion induced by three protein kinase C activators

engagement.model: Dog Folts / ex vivo ADP aggregation (ticagrelor)
engagement.note: Dog/rat ranked ticagrelor above clopidogrel on platelet inhibition; in NSTE-ACS patients 90 mg b.i.d. gave 79% vs 64% IPA.
engagement.short: Ticagrelor > clopidogrel IPA, dog and patients
engagement.quote: AZD6140 exhibited greater mean inhibition of platelet aggregation than a standard regimen of clopidogrel in ACS patients.
engagement.reason: Matched platelet inhibition in ACS patients
engagement.judgement: Juxtaposed: model side is the AstraZeneca dog/rat work (van Giezen 2009, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.thromres.2009.06.029: ticagrelor 63-fold more potent than prasugrel's metabolite on washed human platelets, greater antithrombotic/bleeding separation than clopidogrel in rat and dog) whose primary paper appeared two years after this patient study; the dog studies themselves are dated 2000-2005 in the FDA Brilinta pharmacology review and were summarised in the 2005 van Giezen & Humphries review. A strict reading of rule 5 would put this entry at 2009. Patient side: DISPERSE-2 substudy, 4 weeks, 4 h post-dose IPA clopidogrel 64%, ticagrelor 90 mg 79%, 180 mg 95% (abstract-level). DISPERSE-2 has no ClinicalTrials.gov record (searched by term and by AZD6140 + ACS + 2004-2007 start).

dose.model: Rat dose-response (ex vivo IPA, AV-shunt thrombosis)
dose.note: Rat ED50s (1.2 mg/kg IPA, 0.68 mg/kg thrombosis); clinical doses were set in human IPA studies, no model-vs-patient exposure comparison found.
dose.short: Rat ED50s; no exposure comparison published
dose.quote: CS-747 also exhibited a marked inhibition of ADP-induced ex vivo platelet aggregation in PRP with a rapid onset (<0.5 h) and long duration (>3 days) of action (ED(50) at 4 h=1.2 mg kg(-1)).
dose.judgement: Prasugrel 10 mg/day (~0.14 mg/kg) versus rat ED50 0.68-1.2 mg/kg is a 5-9x species gap nobody published as a comparison; the FDA Brilinta review (p.32) says dog antithrombosis needed 91-99% ex vivo IPA, while the approved ticagrelor dose gave ~79% mean IPA in ACS patients (Storey 2007) and still won PLATO; again no source puts the two side by side, so untested. The FDA Effient (NDA 022307) pharmacology review could not be retrieved (all accessdata URL variants 404), so model_filed for prasugrel is unknown.

efficacy.model: Rat arterial thrombosis (AV-shunt, later FeCl3) and dog Folts
efficacy.note: Clopidogrel's antithrombotic activity was characterised in rat experimental thrombosis models before any ACS trial.
efficacy.quote: aprotinin modified neither the antiaggregating effect of clopidogrel nor its antithrombotic activity, as determined in various experimental models.

efficacy.model: Rat arterial thrombosis (AV-shunt, later FeCl3) and dog Folts
efficacy.note: CURE: clopidogrel cut CV death/MI/stroke 11.4% to 9.3% in 12,562 NSTE-ACS patients, as the rat thrombosis models predicted.
efficacy.quote: The antiplatelet agent clopidogrel has beneficial effects in patients with acute coronary syndromes without ST-segment elevation.
efficacy.judgement: Juxtaposed, direction only. The models' later rankings also held: rat AV-shunt put prasugrel ~9x more potent than clopidogrel (Sugidachi 2000) and TRITON-TIMI 38 showed 9.9% vs 12.1% events (Wiviott 2007, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0706482; NCT00097591 results posted 2010-09-16); rat/dog gave ticagrelor a wider antithrombotic/bleeding window than clopidogrel (van Giezen 2009) and PLATO showed 9.8% vs 11.7% with no rise in overall major bleeding (Wallentin 2009, https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0904327; NCT00391872 results posted 2012-03-13). No P2Y12 antagonist has failed on efficacy in ACS, so 'neg' is unavailable. Selatogrel: rat FeCl3 model predicted equal efficacy with less blood loss than ticagrelor (Rey 2017, https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.338); phase 3 SOS-AMI (NCT04957719) has no results, primary completion 2027-07. CURE predates registry results posting, so registry_date is null.

safety.note: Clopidogrel 5 mg/kg quadrupled rat bleeding time; the bleeding-time model is the class's safety read-out.
safety.quote: 2 hours after a single oral administration, clopidogrel (5 mg/kg, p.o.), induced a 4-fold increase in the bleeding time.

safety.note: CURE: major bleeding 3.7% vs 2.7% with clopidogrel, the direction the bleeding-time models gave.
safety.short: CURE bleeding up, as models said
safety.quote: However, the risk of major bleeding is increased among patients treated with clopidogrel.
safety.judgement: Juxtaposed, direction only. The bleeding ranking also held later: rat bleeding time rose in the same potency order as antithrombosis (Sugidachi 2000) and prasugrel raised TIMI major bleeding 2.4% vs 1.8% in TRITON; dog/rat gave ticagrelor 9.7 vs 2.0 (clopidogrel) separation ratio (van Giezen 2009) and PLATO found no rise in overall major bleeding but more non-CABG bleeding (4.5% vs 3.8%).

safety.model: Rat safety pharmacology (respiration) and dog bleeding time
safety.note: FDA: rat respiratory-rate rise in the 2000 safety-pharmacology study 'manifested in the clinical studies as dyspnea'; dog bleeding separation held in PLATO.
safety.short: FDA: rat breathing signal became dyspnea
safety.quote: The respiratory effects identified in the safety pharmacology studies were manifested in the clinical studies as dyspnea, one of the common adverse effects reported.
safety.judgement: Stated comparison by the FDA reviewer (NDA 22-433, pp. 9 and 36-43): study SR99346-01 (June 2000, rat, 1-100 mg/kg p.o.) raised respiratory rate at all doses before first-in-human; the sponsor only revisited it once clinical dyspnea appeared, and repeat-dose toxicology was not designed to detect it. This contradicts the common claim that animals did not show the ticagrelor dyspnoea signal. Second same-status entry kept deliberately because it is a different model and the only stated (not juxtaposed) comparison in this cell; drop it if the strip must be change-only. Borderline for 'contra': dog cardiovascular safety pharmacology reported arterial-pressure falls and no QT/QTc effect but nothing on heart rate, while DISPERSE-2 found more ventricular pauses >2.5 s (4.3% clopidogrel, 5.5% 90 mg, 9.9% 180 mg; Cannon 2007, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2007.07.053); no source states that animals missed it, so not scored contra. The adenosine-uptake mechanism was modelled in dogs only afterwards (van Giezen 2011, https://doi.org/10.1177/1074248411410883). Selatogrel: rat predicted 2.6-fold less blood loss than ticagrelor (Rey 2017); CCS/AMI patients had no major bleeding but 7% transient dyspnoea (Storey 2020, https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehz807, NCT03384966 results posted 2021-05-17; Sinnaeve 2020, https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jacc.2020.03.059, NCT03487445 results posted 2021-08-25), which the rat work did not address. registry_date is PLATO's, the pivotal trial the review's clinical dyspnea data come from.
